definition_zh: 感觉；知觉；轰动（事件或人）
definition_en: a physical feeling produced by the senses, or a state of great public excitement caused by something
core_image: 外界刺激撞上神经，在身体里亮起一阵可感的反应，随后传遍整群人
scene: 喝下冰水后，牙齿深处突然一阵尖锐的凉意，让人停住： A sharp sensation ran through her teeth as she bit into the ice.
sceneCN: 这里指「身体感觉」（第 1 个义项：由感官刺激产生的身体感受）；句意为她咬到冰块时，一阵尖锐的凉意穿过牙齿。

pos.zh: 感觉；知觉（身体上的感受）
轰动；引起轰动的人或事

derivatives.zh: 引起轰动的；耸人听闻的
耸人听闻的做法；感觉主义

senses.title: A physical feeling
senses.titleCN: 身体感觉：由刺激产生的一阵感受
senses.definition: a feeling in the body produced by something acting on the senses or on the nerves
senses.definitionCN: 由作用于感官或神经的刺激在身体中产生的感受
senses.example: A sharp sensation ran through her teeth as she bit into the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 她咬到冰块时，一阵尖锐的凉意穿过牙齿。
senses.why: The word names what is felt rather than what is sensed: the stimulus is outside, and the sensation is the body's response.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名「被感受到的东西」而非「被感知的对象」：刺激在外，感觉是身体的回应。

senses.title: Sensation and perception
senses.titleCN: 感觉（与知觉相对的概念）
senses.definition: the raw impression received by the senses, as studied in psychology before interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中未经解释、由感官接收的原始印象
senses.example: Psychology separates sensation from perception, the meaning given to it.
senses.exampleCN: 心理学把感觉与赋予其意义的知觉区分开来。
senses.why: In this technical pair, sensation is the input before the mind labels it, which is why the two words are always taught together.
senses.whyCN: 在这一技术配对中，「感觉」是心智贴标签之前的输入，因此两个词总是成对讲授。

senses.title: A public stir
senses.titleCN: 轰动：引起众人关注的事件
senses.definition: a sudden wave of public excitement or surprise caused by an event, a person or a work
senses.definitionCN: 由事件、人物或作品引起的突然而广泛的公众激动或惊讶
senses.example: The young pianist caused a sensation at her first concert.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻钢琴家在她的首场音乐会上引起轰动。
senses.why: The bodily meaning is transferred to a crowd: excitement runs through people the way a feeling runs through nerves.
senses.whyCN: 身体义被转用到人群：激动穿过众人，正如感觉穿过神经。

senses.title: A hit or a wonder
senses.definition: a person or work that becomes suddenly and widely famous
senses.definitionCN: 突然广为人知、红极一时的人或作品
senses.example: The novel was the sensation of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说是当季最轰动的话题。
senses.why: The cause and the effect change places: the thing that produces the stir comes to be called the sensation itself.
senses.whyCN: 因果位置互换：引起轰动的事物本身也被称为「轰动」。

senses.title: Loss of sensation
senses.titleCN: 感觉丧失：身体某处不再有感受
senses.definition: the condition in which a part of the body can no longer feel touch, heat or pain
senses.definitionCN: 身体某部位不再能感受触、热或痛的状态
senses.example: Loss of sensation in the fingers can be a sign of nerve damage.
senses.exampleCN: 手指失去感觉可能是神经受损的迹象。
senses.why: The absence is defined against the presence: what is missing is exactly the feeling the word normally names.
senses.whyCN: 缺失是相对存在来定义的：失去的正是这个词通常所指的那种感受。

senses.title: Tactile sensation
senses.definition: the feeling produced when something touches or presses on the skin
senses.definitionCN: 某物接触或压迫皮肤时产生的感受
senses.example: Tactile sensation tells the hand how rough the stone is.
senses.exampleCN: 触觉告诉手这块石头有多粗糙。
senses.why: Each sense contributes its own kind of sensation, so the word is often paired with the channel that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 每种感官贡献自己的一类感觉，因此这个词常与产生它的通道搭配。

senses.title: Physiological reception
senses.titleCN: 生理学意义上的感觉接收
senses.definition: the process by which a receptor turns a stimulus into a nerve signal
senses.definitionCN: 感受器把刺激转成神经信号的过程
senses.example: The study measured sensation at the level of single receptors.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究在单个感受器层面测量感觉。
senses.why: At this level sensation is not yet a conscious feeling but the event of conversion that makes feeling possible.
senses.whyCN: 在这一层面，感觉还不是意识到的感受，而是使感受成为可能的转换事件。

senses.title: A feeling of unease
senses.titleCN: 某种抽象感受（不安、沉重）
senses.definition: a vague emotional or bodily impression, such as a sensation of dread or of weight
senses.definitionCN: 模糊的情绪或身体印象，如不安或沉重之感
senses.example: He woke with a sensation of dread he could not explain.
senses.exampleCN: 他醒来时有一种说不出的不安感。
senses.why: The word extends from concrete feeling to any impression that seems to arrive from outside the will.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从具体感受扩展到一切仿佛不请自来的印象。

intro.en: Sensation comes from Late Latin sensatio, built on sensus, the past participle of sentire to feel, and came into English through French. The public-stir sense is later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sensation 来自晚期拉丁 sensatio，建立在 sensus（sentire「感觉」的过去分词）之上，经法语进入英语。轰动义出现较晚。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel or perceive, and sensus named the feeling that results.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉或感知，sensus 指由此产生的感受。

items.en: Late Latin sensatio named the act or state of feeling; the suffix -tio marks a process or its result.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 sensatio 指感觉的动作或状态；后缀 -tio 标记过程或其结果。

items.en: French sensation carried the word into English in the seventeenth century, first in medical and philosophical writing.
items.cn: 法语 sensation 在 17 世纪把这个词带入英语，最初见于医学与哲学写作。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century psychology fixed the pair sensation and perception as separate stages.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪心理学把 sensation 与 perception 固定为两个不同阶段。

items.en: The sense of a public sensation developed in the eighteenth century, when newspapers began to report events as waves of excitement.
items.cn: 指公众轰动的义项在 18 世纪发展起来，当时报纸开始把事件报道为一阵阵激动。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first English use of sensation is not firmly dated, and the exact point at which the public sense separated from the medical one is unclear.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：sensation 最早的英语书证没有确切年代，公众义从医学义中分出的确切时点也不清楚。

note.en: The first group holds same-root nouns and adjectives that are easily confused; the second holds words for related experiences.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、易混的名词与形容词；第二组是表示相近体验的词。

entries.definition: The general faculty of feeling or the meaning of a word; sensation is one specific feeling produced through it.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指感觉能力或词义；sensation 是通过它产生的一次具体感受。

entries.definition: Relating to the senses; it describes the channel, while sensation names what passes through it.
entries.definitionCN: 与感官有关的；它描述通道，而 sensation 命名通过通道的东西。

entries.definition: Causing or intended to cause a stir; it is the adjective of the public sense, not of bodily feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 引起或意图引起轰动的；它是公众义的形容词，而非身体感觉的形容词。

entries.definition: A view shaped by emotion; it also comes from sentire, but through a different Latin noun, and it means opinion or feeling rather than bodily sensation.
entries.definitionCN: 受情感影响的看法；同出 sentire，但经另一个拉丁名词，意为看法或情感，而非身体感受。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for any bodily or emotional experience; sensation is its more technical or vivid counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何身体或情绪体验的日常词；sensation 是更技术或更鲜明的对应词。

entries.definition: The meaning the mind gives to what the senses deliver; sensation is the raw impression before that meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 心智赋予感官内容的意义；sensation 是意义之前的原始印象。

entries.definition: A general effect left on the mind or senses; it is vaguer and less physical than sensation.
entries.definitionCN: 留在心智或感官上的一般印象；比 sensation 更模糊、更少身体性。

entries.definition: A sudden wave of excitement; it is close to the public sense of sensation but always pleasurable.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的一阵兴奋；接近 sensation 的公众义，但总带有愉悦。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin process noun, the real psychology pair and the real newspaper phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁过程名词、真实的心理学配对与真实的报纸短语。

normal.en: Sensus is feeling, and -atio marks a process, so sensation is the event of feeling something.
normal.cn: sensus 是感觉，-atio 标记过程，因此 sensation 是「感觉到某物」这一事件。

normal.en: Psychology teaches sensation first and perception second: raw input, then meaning.
normal.cn: 心理学先讲 sensation 后讲 perception：先原始输入，后意义。

normal.en: Cause a sensation is the fixed newspaper phrase for a public stir.
normal.cn: cause a sensation 是报纸上表示「引起轰动」的固定说法。

normal.en: Loss of sensation is the clinical phrase for numbness or nerve damage.
normal.cn: loss of sensation 是表示麻木或神经损伤的临床说法。

normal.en: The adjective splits in two: sensory for the channel, sensational for the stir.
normal.cn: 形容词分成两条：sensory 指通道，sensational 指轰动。

abstract.en: Picture a struck bell: the blow is outside, the ring is inside the body.
abstract.cn: 想象一口被敲响的钟：敲击在外，余音在身体里。

abstract.en: Picture a wave crossing a crowd: one person feels it, then everyone feels it.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵波穿过人群：先是一个人感到，然后所有人都感到。

abstract.en: Picture a switch that can also be off: numbness is the same circuit with no current.
abstract.cn: 想象一个也能关闭的开关：麻木就是同一条电路断了电流。

examples.en: A burning sensation in the chest should be checked by a doctor.
examples.cn: 胸部灼热感应当请医生检查。

examples.en: The invention caused a sensation at the 1900 world fair.
examples.cn: 这项发明在 1900 年世界博览会上引起轰动。

examples.en: The drug reduces sensation in the skin before surgery.
examples.cn: 这种药在手术前降低皮肤的感觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三筛神」（sensation）——三层筛选后，神经感到的那一下 → 感觉；轰动

root: 晚期拉丁 sensatio「感觉（过程或状态）」，来自 sensus（sentire「感觉、感知」的过去分词）；经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a single bodily feeling to the psychological concept, then out into public excitement, a famous work, numbness, touch, receptor-level reception, and finally a vague impression of dread.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一次身体感受出发，到心理学概念，再走向公众轰动、成名作品、麻木、触觉、感受器层面的接收，最后是模糊的不安印象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stimulus strikes a nerve and a felt response lights up inside the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：刺激撞上神经，身体内部亮起一阵可感的回应。

branches.en: LOSS AND TOUCH: feeling can vanish, and one channel still delivers it.
branches.cn: 丧失与触觉：感觉会消失，而某个通道仍能传递它。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL LADDER: the psychological input and the receptor event beneath it.
branches.cn: 技术阶梯：心理学的输入概念，以及其下感受器层面的事件。

branches.en: THE WONDER: the thing itself becomes famous overnight.
branches.cn: 轰动之物：那件事物本身一夜之间人尽皆知。

branches.en: VAGUE IMPRESSION: a feeling that arrives without a clear source.
branches.cn: 模糊印象：没有明确来源却出现的感受。

branches.en: ONE METAPHOR, TWO SCALES: nerves and crowds both conduct a wave of feeling.
branches.cn: 一个比喻两种尺度：神经与人群都在传导一阵感受。

intro.en: Sensation is a Latin process noun: the stem sens- plus -ation, the English form of Latin -tio.
intro.cn: sensation 是拉丁过程名词：词干 sens- 加 -ation，即拉丁 -tio 的英语形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire gives sensus and sensatio; the adjective sensualis and the noun sentimentum belong to neighbouring branches of the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire 衍生 sensus 与 sensatio；形容词 sensualis 与名词 sentimentum 属于同一词族的邻近支线。

items.example: The whole family rests on this verb.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族都建立在这个动词上。

items.example: Sensus is the noun behind sense.
items.exampleCN: sensus 是 sense 背后的名词。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a noun of process.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: A sharp sensation ran through her teeth.
items.exampleCN: 一阵尖锐的感觉穿过她的牙齿。

items.example: Sensory nerves carry the signal inward.
items.exampleCN: 感觉神经把信号向体内传导。

items.example: The paper was accused of sensationalism.
items.exampleCN: 这家报纸被指刻意耸人听闻。

items.meaning: able to be felt; also reasonable
items.exampleCN: 这点差别几乎感觉不到。

items.example: The scarred skin was insensitive to touch.
items.exampleCN: 留疤的皮肤对触摸不敏感。

definition_zh: 感觉；意义；理智；感觉到
definition_en: a feeling from the body, the meaning of something, good judgment, or to become aware of something
core_image: 指尖轻轻碰到杯壁，热度顺着皮肤传上来
scene: 她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。She sensed that something was wrong in the room.
sceneCN: 这里 sensed 是「感觉到」（第 4 个义项）；句意：她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。

senses.title: Body feeling
senses.definition: a feeling produced by the senses
senses.definitionCN: 由感官产生的感觉
senses.example: She felt a sense of warmth from the cup.
senses.exampleCN: 她从杯子上感到一阵暖意。
senses.why: This is the basic sensory sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的感官义。

senses.title: Meaning
senses.definition: the meaning that words or actions carry
senses.definitionCN: 词语或行为所承载的意义
senses.example: I cannot make sense of this sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 我弄不懂这个句子的意思。
senses.why: Meaning is what the mind grasps.
senses.whyCN: 意义是心智所把握的东西。

senses.title: Good judgment
senses.definition: practical good judgment
senses.definitionCN: 实际而良好的判断力
senses.example: It is common sense to lock the door.
senses.exampleCN: 锁门是常识。
senses.why: The mind's sense becomes sound judgment.
senses.whyCN: 心智的感觉变成健全的判断。

senses.title: To become aware
senses.definition: to become aware of something without being told
senses.definitionCN: 未经告知而察觉到某事
senses.example: She sensed that something was wrong in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of perceiving.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为感知的动作。

intro.en: Sense comes from Latin sentire, to feel, through Latin sensus, a feeling.
intro.cn: sense 出自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），经拉丁语 sensus（感觉）而来。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel or perceive.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉或察觉。

items.en: Sensus named a feeling or meaning.
items.cn: sensus 指感觉或意义。

items.en: Sens carried both feeling and meaning.
items.cn: sens 兼具感觉与意义。

items.en: Sense added the idea of good judgment.
items.cn: sense 增加了良好判断之义。

items.en: Make sense became a common phrase.
items.cn: make sense 成为常用短语。

note.en: Sense is compared with similar-looking words and with words for feeling and meaning.
note.cn: 把 sense 与形近词以及表示感觉和意义的词作比较。

entries.definition: from a past time until now

normalIntro.en: Sense covers what the body feels, what words mean, and what the mind judges.
normalIntro.cn: sense 涵盖身体所感、词语所表与心智所判。

normal.en: We have five senses.
A sentence must make sense.
Common sense is judgment without special training.
normal.cn: 常识是无需专门训练的判断力。

normal.en: She sensed danger before she saw it.
normal.cn: 她在看见危险之前就察觉到了。

normal.en: In a sense, both answers are right.
normal.cn: 在某种意义上，两个答案都对。

abstract.en: Meaning is the shape a feeling takes when it is shared.
abstract.cn: 意义是感觉被分享时呈现的形状。

abstract.en: Good judgment is feeling trained by experience.
abstract.cn: 良好的判断力是被经验训练过的感觉。

abstract.en: We notice most what we have learned to sense.
abstract.cn: 我们最容易察觉自己学会去感受的东西。

examples.en: She sensed that something was wrong in the room.
examples.cn: 她感觉到房间里有些不对劲。

examples.en: I cannot make sense of this sentence.
examples.cn: 我弄不懂这个句子的意思。

examples.en: It is common sense to lock the door.
examples.cn: 锁门是常识。

dict_mnemonic.text: sense 出自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），本义「感官所感」，后扩展为意义、判断力与察觉。

root: 源自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），核心义「感知与领会」。

sensesIntro.en: Sense means a body feeling, a meaning, good judgment, or the act of perceiving.
sensesIntro.cn: sense 意为身体感觉、意义、理智或察觉。

core.en: The mind and body taking in what is there.
core.cn: 身心对眼前之物的接收。

branches.en: Warmth, smell, or sound received by the body.
branches.cn: 身体接收到的热、气味或声音。

branches.en: What a sentence or action means.
branches.cn: 句子或行为所表达的意思。

branches.en: Practical judgment about daily life.
branches.cn: 关于日常生活的实际判断。

branches.en: Noticing something before being told.
branches.cn: 在被告知之前就注意到某事。

branches.en: Feeling and noticing are two sides of one act.
branches.cn: 感受与察觉是同一动作的两面。

intro.en: Sense belongs to the Latin sentire family of feeling and perceiving.
intro.cn: sense 属于拉丁语 sentire（感觉）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire and sensus are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sentire 与 sensus 是历史词根。

items.example: He has a sense of duty.

items.exampleCN: 这个设备正在感应运动。

items.example: The cold caused a burning sensation.

definition_zh: 明智的；合理的；可察觉的
definition_en: showing good judgment, based on reason, or able to be noticed
core_image: 雨天门口放着一把伞，出门的人顺手拿了起来
scene: 在暴风雨中待在家里是明智的。It is sensible to stay home during a storm.
sceneCN: 这里 sensible 是「明智的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：在暴风雨中待在家里是明智的。

senses.title: Showing good judgment
senses.definition: showing practical good judgment
senses.definitionCN: 表现出实际而良好的判断力
senses.example: It is sensible to stay home during a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 在暴风雨中待在家里是明智的。
senses.why: This is the most common modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最常见的义项。

senses.title: Based on reason
senses.definition: based on reason rather than emotion
senses.definitionCN: 基于理性而非情绪
senses.example: She gave a sensible explanation.
senses.exampleCN: 她给出了一个合理的解释。
senses.why: Good judgment rests on reason.
senses.whyCN: 良好判断建立在理性之上。

senses.title: Able to be noticed
senses.definition: able to be perceived by the senses
senses.definitionCN: 能被感官察觉的
senses.example: The change was hardly sensible to the eye.
senses.exampleCN: 这种变化肉眼几乎察觉不到。
senses.why: This is the older sense of being felt.
senses.whyCN: 这是较古老的可被感知义。

intro.en: Sensible comes from Latin sensibilis, able to be felt, from sentire, to feel.
intro.cn: sensible 出自拉丁语 sensibilis（可被感知的），源于 sentire（感觉）。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel or perceive.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉或察觉。

items.en: Sensibilis meant able to be felt.
items.cn: sensibilis 意为可被感知的。

items.en: Old French sensible kept the sense of sensitive.
items.cn: 古法语 sensible 保留了易感的含义。

items.en: English sensible first meant capable of being felt.
items.cn: 英语 sensible 最初意为可被感知的。

items.en: It shifted toward good judgment.
items.cn: 它逐渐转向表示良好判断。

note.en: Sensible is compared with similar-looking words and with words for good judgment.
note.cn: 把 sensible 与形近词以及表示良好判断的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sensible means able to be felt, then able to be trusted as sound judgment.
normalIntro.cn: sensible 原意可被感知，后指判断可靠、明智。

normal.en: A sensible decision is easy to explain.
Sensible shoes are made for walking.
normal.cn: 实用舒适的鞋是为走路做的。

normal.en: The adverb is sensibly.
Sensible people plan before they act.
normal.cn: 明智的人先计划再行动。

normal.en: The older sense survives in insensible.
normal.cn: 较古老的含义保留在 insensible 中。

abstract.en: Good judgment is a sense shared with others.
abstract.cn: 良好的判断力是一种与他人共享的感知。

abstract.en: What can be felt can often be understood.

core.en: Feeling turned into sound judgment.

definition_zh: 敏感的；体贴的；易受影响的；灵敏的
definition_en: quick to feel or react, careful about others' feelings, easily affected, or able to detect small changes
core_image: 一片叶子碰到手指就迅速卷起，像被轻轻惊到
scene: 她的皮肤对阳光很敏感。Her skin is sensitive to sunlight.
sceneCN: 这里 sensitive 是「敏感的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她的皮肤对阳光很敏感。

senses.title: Quick to react
senses.definition: reacting quickly to small changes or touches
senses.definitionCN: 对细微变化或触碰反应迅速
senses.example: Her skin is sensitive to sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 她的皮肤对阳光很敏感。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的身体义。

senses.title: Careful of others
senses.definition: aware of and careful about other people's feelings
senses.definitionCN: 体察并照顾他人的感受
senses.example: He is sensitive to his friends' moods.
senses.exampleCN: 他很体察朋友们的情绪。
senses.why: Feeling quickly extends to social feeling.
senses.whyCN: 感受迅速延伸到社交情感。

senses.title: Easily affected
senses.definition: easily harmed or changed by something
senses.definitionCN: 容易受到某物伤害或影响
senses.example: The market is sensitive to bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 市场对坏消息很敏感。
senses.why: A sensitive thing reacts strongly to change.
senses.whyCN: 敏感之物对变化反应强烈。

senses.title: Able to detect
senses.definition: able to measure or notice very small changes
senses.definitionCN: 能够测量或察觉极小的变化
senses.example: The instrument is sensitive to heat.
senses.exampleCN: 这台仪器对热很灵敏。
senses.why: Instruments borrow the same responsiveness.
senses.whyCN: 仪器借用了同样的反应能力。

intro.en: Sensitive comes from Latin sensitivus, having feeling, from sentire, to feel.
intro.cn: sensitive 出自拉丁语 sensitivus（有感觉的），源于 sentire（感觉）。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉。

items.en: Sensitivus meant having feeling.
items.cn: sensitivus 意为有感觉的。

items.en: The word named parts able to feel.
items.cn: 该词指能够感觉的部位。

items.en: Sensitive extended to feelings and issues.
items.cn: sensitive 扩展到情感与议题。

items.en: It also describes delicate instruments.
items.cn: 它也用来形容精密的仪器。

note.en: Sensitive is compared with similar-looking words and with words for responsiveness.
note.cn: 把 sensitive 与形近词以及表示反应能力的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Sensitive means quick to feel, whether skin, people, markets, or machines.
normalIntro.cn: sensitive 意为容易感受，无论皮肤、人、市场还是机器。

normal.en: Sensitive skin burns easily.
A sensitive friend notices your mood.
normal.cn: 体贴的朋友会察觉你的情绪。

normal.en: Prices are sensitive to supply.
The adverb is sensitively.
The opposite is insensitive.

abstract.en: To be sensitive is to let the world in.
abstract.cn: 敏感就是让世界进来。

abstract.en: A fine instrument hears what a coarse one cannot.
abstract.cn: 精细的仪器能听见粗糙仪器听不到的东西。

abstract.en: Care for others begins with noticing them.
abstract.cn: 对他人的关怀始于注意到他们。

examples.en: Her skin is sensitive to sunlight.
examples.cn: 她的皮肤对阳光很敏感。

examples.en: He is sensitive to his friends' moods.
examples.cn: 他很体察朋友们的情绪。

root: 源自拉丁语 sentire（感觉），核心义「容易感受与反应」。

sensesIntro.en: Sensitive means quick to react, careful of others, easily affected, or able to detect small changes.

core.en: Responding strongly to small things.
core.cn: 对细微之物反应强烈。

branches.en: Skin or senses that react fast.
branches.cn: 反应快速的身体或感官。

branches.en: A person who notices feelings.
A system easily moved by events.
A device that detects tiny changes.
Body and heart share one responsiveness.
branches.cn: 身体与心灵共享一种反应力。

intro.en: Sensitive belongs to the Latin sentire family of feeling.
intro.cn: sensitive 属于拉丁语 sentire（感觉）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin sensitivus and sentire are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sensitivus 与 sentire 是历史词根。

items.example: The area is sensitive to touch.

items.example: She has a keen sense of smell.

definition_zh: 感觉的；感官的；感觉信息的
definition_en: relating to the senses, or to the organs and nerves that receive information from the world
core_image: 一排朝外的小天线，把光、声、热、压力转成身体能读的信号
scene: 婴儿第一次摸到粗糙的毛毯，手指缩了一下，脸上露出惊讶： The baby's sensory system registered the rough texture at once.
sceneCN: 这里指「感觉的、与感官有关的」（第 1 个义项：涉及感觉接收与传导）；句意为婴儿的感觉系统立刻觉察到毛毯粗糙的质地。

pos.zh: 感觉信息的；由感官接收的

senses.title: Relating to the senses
senses.definition: concerning the senses or the process of receiving impressions through them
senses.definitionCN: 关于感觉，或关于通过感官接收印象的过程
senses.example: The baby's sensory system registered the rough texture at once.
senses.exampleCN: 婴儿的感觉系统立刻觉察到粗糙的质地。
senses.why: The adjective marks whatever belongs to the channel from world to body, so it points at the receiving side rather than the thinking side.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记从外界到身体这条通道上的一切，因此指向接收端而非思考端。

senses.title: Of the sense organs
senses.definition: belonging to organs such as the eyes, ears and skin that receive stimuli
senses.definitionCN: 属于眼、耳、皮肤等接收刺激的器官
senses.example: Sensory organs line the surface of the body and open into it.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉器官分布在体表，并向体内开口。
senses.why: Organs are the hardware of feeling, so the adjective attaches to the structures that face the outside world.
senses.whyCN: 器官是感觉的硬件，因此这个形容词附着在那些朝向外部世界的结构上。

senses.title: Of sensory nerves
senses.definition: relating to the nerves that carry signals from the body toward the brain
senses.definitionCN: 与把信号从身体传向脑的神经有关的
senses.example: A sensory nerve carries the signal from the fingertip to the spine.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉神经把信号从指尖传到脊柱。
senses.why: Once the signal leaves the organ it travels on a nerve, and the same adjective follows it inward.
senses.whyCN: 信号离开器官后由神经运输，同一个形容词也随之前行。

senses.title: Sensory input
senses.titleCN: 感觉输入：进入身体的信息
senses.definition: information coming into the body through the senses, treated as data
senses.definitionCN: 通过感官进入身体、被当作数据处理的信息
senses.example: Too much sensory input can overwhelm a small child.
senses.exampleCN: 过多的感觉输入会让幼童难以承受。
senses.why: The engineering metaphor turns feeling into a stream of signals, which is why input is the usual partner of sensory.
senses.whyCN: 工程比喻把感觉变成一股信号流，因此「输入」是这个形容词最常见的搭配。

senses.title: Sensory experience
senses.titleCN: 感官体验：由五种感觉组成的经历
senses.definition: an experience built from what can be seen, heard, touched, tasted or smelled
senses.definitionCN: 由视觉、听觉、触觉、味觉或嗅觉构成的体验
senses.example: The museum designs a sensory experience rather than a lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 这座博物馆设计的是感官体验，而非讲座。
senses.why: Here the adjective describes a whole event that is addressed to the body rather than to knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 这里的形容词描述一整段面向身体的经历，而不是面向知识。

senses.title: Sensory evaluation of food
senses.definition: the professional testing of food by taste, smell, appearance and texture
senses.definitionCN: 靠味、嗅、外观与质地进行的食品专业测试
senses.example: Trained panellists carry out sensory evaluation of the new bread.
senses.exampleCN: 受训的评审员对新面包进行感官评价。
senses.why: Industry uses the word because the instrument is a human sense organ, and the measurement is what the senses report.
senses.whyCN: 行业使用这个词，因为仪器就是人的感官，测量结果就是感官所报告的东西。

senses.title: Sensory processing
senses.titleCN: 感觉加工：大脑整理信号的过程
senses.definition: the way the nervous system sorts, combines and interprets signals from the senses
senses.definitionCN: 神经系统对来自感官的信号进行分类、合并与解释的方式
senses.example: Sensory processing difficulties make noise feel painful.
senses.exampleCN: 感觉加工困难会让噪声变得难以忍受。
senses.why: The focus moves from reception to handling: signals are taken in, then sorted by the brain.
senses.whyCN: 焦点从接收转到处理：信号被接收后由脑整理。

senses.title: Sensory overload or deprivation
senses.definition: states in which the senses receive far too much stimulation or almost none
senses.definitionCN: 感官受到过多刺激或几乎没有刺激的状态
senses.example: Sensory deprivation in a silent room can distort time.
senses.exampleCN: 在无声房间里的感觉剥夺会扭曲时间感。
senses.why: Both extremes test the same channel, so the adjective marks conditions defined by the amount of incoming signal.
senses.whyCN: 两个极端考验的都是同一条通道，因此这个形容词标记由输入量多少来定义的状态。

intro.en: Sensory is sense plus the Latin suffix -orius, from Latin sensorius, built on sensus, the past participle of sentire to feel. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sensory 由 sense 加拉丁后缀 -orius 构成，源头为拉丁 sensorius，建立在 sensus（sentire「感觉」的过去分词）之上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel, perceive or think, and its past participle sensus supplied the noun for feeling and the root of the whole family.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉、感知或思考，其过去分词 sensus 提供表示感觉的名词，也是整个词族的词根。

items.en: The relational adjective sensorius meant belonging to feeling or to the seat of feeling; it survives mainly through English sensory.
items.cn: 关系形容词 sensorius 意为属于感觉或感觉中枢的，主要通过英语 sensory 留存下来。

items.en: Sense entered English through Old French sens, and the adjective sensory appears in English writing by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: sense 经古法语 sens 进入英语，形容词 sensory 在 17 世纪的英语写作中出现。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology split the nervous system into sensory and motor sides, fixing the modern technical use.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学把神经系统分为感觉侧与运动侧，确立了现代技术用法。

items.en: Psychology extended the word to input, processing and experience, so sensory now covers far more than the organs themselves.
items.cn: 心理学把这个词扩展到输入、加工与体验，因此 sensory 现在涵盖的范围远大于器官本身。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first English use of sensory is not firmly dated, and the earlier Medieval Latin status of sensorius is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：sensory 最早的英语书证没有确切年代，sensorius 在中世纪拉丁语中的使用状况也有争议。

note.en: The first group contains words built on the same root that are routinely confused; the second contains adjectives with a similar feel.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、常被混淆的词；第二组是语感相近的形容词。

entries.definition: Appealing to the senses in a rich, pleasurable way; it praises the experience rather than describing the nerve pathway.
entries.definitionCN: 以丰富愉悦的方式取悦感官；它赞美体验，而非描述神经通路。

entries.definition: Relating to bodily pleasure, often sexual; it is about desire, not about sensory reception.
entries.definitionCN: 与身体快感有关，常指情欲；它讲欲望，而非感觉接收。

entries.definition: A device that detects a physical quantity; a sensor is a machine, while sensory describes a living system.
entries.definitionCN: 检测物理量的装置；sensor 是机器，sensory 描述活体系统。

entries.definition: An official who removes objectionable material; it sounds like sensor but comes from a different Latin verb meaning to assess.
entries.definitionCN: 删除不当内容的官员；读音像 sensor，但来自另一个意为「评估」的拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Relating to perception, the process of recognising what the senses deliver; sensory is the input, perceptual is the interpretation.
entries.definitionCN: 与知觉有关的，即识别感官所给内容的过程；sensory 是输入，perceptual 是解释。

entries.definition: Relating to touch; it names one sense, while sensory covers all of them.
entries.definitionCN: 与触觉有关的；它只指一种感觉，而 sensory 涵盖全部。

entries.definition: Relating to nerves; sensory signals travel on neural pathways, but neural does not itself mean felt.
entries.definitionCN: 与神经有关的；感觉信号走神经通路，但 neural 本身不表示「被感觉到」。

entries.definition: Quick to detect or react to small changes; it describes a capacity, not the whole sensory system.
entries.definitionCN: 对微小变化反应敏锐；它描述一种能力，而非整个感觉系统。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin participle, the real physiology split and the real industry phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁分词、真实的生理学分工与真实的行业短语。

normal.en: Sensus is the past participle of sentire to feel, so sensory means belonging to feeling.
normal.cn: sensus 是 sentire「感觉」的过去分词，因此 sensory 意为「属于感觉的」。

normal.en: Physiology pairs sensory with motor: signals come in on one side and commands go out on the other.
normal.cn: 生理学把 sensory 与 motor 配对：信号从一侧进入，指令从另一侧发出。

normal.en: Sensory input, sensory processing and sensory overload trace a signal from door to brain to breakdown.
normal.cn: sensory input、sensory processing、sensory overload 串起信号从入口到大脑再到过载的全过程。

normal.en: Sensory evaluation is the food industry phrase for judging with eyes, nose, tongue and teeth.
normal.cn: sensory evaluation 是食品行业用语，指用眼、鼻、舌与牙齿作评判。

normal.en: The same root gives sense, sensation, sensible and sensor, so the family can be read from one stem.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 sense、sensation、sensible 与 sensor，因此整个词族可由一个词干读出。

abstract.en: Picture a row of small antennae facing outward, each tuned to one kind of weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一排朝外的小天线，每一根只对一种天气敏感。

abstract.en: Picture a doorway that is also a filter: everything enters, but only some of it is let through.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门同时是过滤器：一切都来到门口，只有一部分被放行。

abstract.en: Picture a volume knob turned to maximum and then to zero; both extremes test the same channel.
abstract.cn: 想象一个音量旋钮先拧到最大再拧到零：两个极端考验的是同一条通道。

examples.en: Sensory nerves carry information from the skin to the brain.
examples.cn: 感觉神经把信息从皮肤传到大脑。

examples.en: The room was designed to reduce sensory input for autistic children.
examples.cn: 这个房间的设计目的是为自闭症儿童减少感觉输入。

examples.en: A trained panel performed a sensory evaluation of the cheese.
examples.cn: 一个受训评审组对这款奶酪做了感官评价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「三色瑞」（sensory）——三种颜色都靠眼睛去感觉 → 感觉的；感官的

root: 拉丁 sensorius「属于感觉的」，来自 sensus（sentire「感觉、感知」的过去分词）；sentire 的印欧祖形为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run along one channel: the senses in general, the organs, the nerves, the incoming data, the experience, the professional test, the processing, and the extremes of too much or too little.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条通道展开：泛指感觉、器官、神经、输入的数据、体验、专业测试、加工过程，以及过多与过少的两个极端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: antennae facing the world, turning light, sound and pressure into readable signals.
core.cn: 核心意象：朝向世界的天线，把光、声与压力转成可读的信号。

branches.en: THE ORGANS: eyes, ears and skin that face the world.
branches.cn: 这些器官：面对外部世界的眼、耳与皮肤。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL'S TRIP: nerves carry it inward, input names it as data.
branches.cn: 信号的行进：神经把它带入体内，「输入」把它命名为数据。

branches.en: TWO USES OF THE SAME WORD: a personal experience, and a professional test of a product.
branches.cn: 同一个词的两种用法：个人的体验，以及对产品的专业测试。

branches.en: THE LOAD: too much or too little stimulation breaks the system.
branches.cn: 负荷：刺激过多或过少都会让系统失灵。

branches.en: FROM WORLD TO MIND: the same adjective covers reception and the processing that follows.
branches.cn: 从世界到心智：同一个形容词既涵盖接收，也涵盖随后的加工。

intro.en: Sensory is a Latin relational adjective in -orius; the stem sens- also builds sense, sensation, sensible and sensor.
intro.cn: sensory 是带 -orius 的拉丁关系形容词；词干 sens- 还构成 sense、sensation、sensible 与 sensor。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire feel gives sensus feeling and sensorius of feeling; English also borrowed sensorium, the seat of the senses, from Late Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire「感觉」衍生 sensus「感觉」与 sensorius「属于感觉的」；英语还从晚期拉丁语借入 sensorium「感觉中枢」。

items.example: The verb covers both bodily feeling and opinion.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词既指身体感觉，也指看法。

items.example: Sensus is the source of sense and sensation.
items.exampleCN: sensus 是 sense 与 sensation 的来源。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into an adjective of relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成关系形容词。
感觉输入塑造早期学习。

items.example: A sharp sensation ran through her teeth.
items.exampleCN: 一阵尖锐的感觉穿过她的牙齿。

items.example: The sensor records temperature every minute.
items.exampleCN: 传感器每分钟记录一次温度。

items.meaning: the seat or system of the senses
items.example: The sensorium gathers signals from the whole body.
items.exampleCN: 感觉系统汇集来自全身的信号。

items.example: Sensorineural hearing loss affects the inner ear.
items.exampleCN: 感音神经性听力损失影响内耳。

items.meaning: judging a product by the senses
items.example: Sensory evaluation scored the bread on texture.
items.exampleCN: 感官评价给面包的质地打了分。

definition_zh: 句子；判决；宣判
definition_en: a group of words that expresses a complete idea, a punishment given by a court, or to order a punishment
core_image: 纸上写着一行完整的字，末尾落下一个句点
scene: 他写了一个很长的句子。He wrote a very long sentence.
sceneCN: 这里 sentence 是「句子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他写了一个很长的句子。

senses.title: Group of words
senses.definition: a group of words that expresses a complete thought
senses.definitionCN: 表达完整思想的一组词
senses.example: He wrote a very long sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他写了一个很长的句子。
senses.why: This is the grammar sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是语法义。

senses.title: Court punishment
senses.definition: a punishment ordered by a court
senses.definitionCN: 法庭判处的惩罚
senses.example: The judge gave him a light sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 法官给了他轻判。
senses.why: A court's judgment is also called a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 法庭的判断也叫 sentence。

senses.title: To order punishment
senses.definition: to order a punishment in court

intro.en: Sentence comes from Latin sententia, an opinion or judgment, from sentire, to feel.
intro.cn: sentence 出自拉丁语 sententia（意见、判断），源于 sentire（感觉）。

items.en: Sentire meant to feel or think.
items.cn: sentire 意为感觉或思考。

items.en: Sententia meant an opinion or judgment.
items.cn: sententia 意为意见或判断。

items.en: Old French sentence kept the judgment sense.
items.cn: 古法语 sentence 保留了判断义。

items.en: English sentence meant opinion or legal judgment.
items.cn: 英语 sentence 意为意见或法律判决。

items.en: The grammar sense became dominant.
items.cn: 语法义后来占据主导。

note.en: Sentence is compared with similar-looking words and with grammar and law words.

normalIntro.en: Sentence is a complete thought in words, and also a court's judgment.
normalIntro.cn: sentence 是用词语表达的完整思想，也是法庭的判决。

normal.en: A sentence begins with a capital letter.
A topic sentence states the main idea.
A life sentence lasts many years.
The judge passed sentence at noon.
Sentence and sentiment share a root.

abstract.en: A sentence closes a thought the way a door closes a room.
abstract.cn: 句子结束一个思想，就像门关上一个房间。

abstract.en: Judgment and grammar both put things in order.
abstract.cn: 判决与语法都在给事物排定秩序。

abstract.en: The same word can hold a thought or a punishment.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能装思想，也能装惩罚。

examples.en: He wrote a very long sentence.

examples.en: The judge gave him a light sentence.
examples.cn: 法官给了他轻判。

examples.en: The court sentenced him to two years.
examples.cn: 法庭判处他两年徒刑。

dict_mnemonic.text: sentence 出自拉丁语 sententia（意见、判断），源于 sentire（感觉、思考），本义「所想的判断」，后兼指语法句子与法庭判决。

sensesIntro.cn: sentence 意为完整的句子、法庭判决或宣判。

core.en: A complete judgment, in words or in law.
core.cn: 用言语或法律作出的完整判断。

branches.en: Words closing into one complete idea.
branches.cn: 收束成一个完整思想的词语。

The act of declaring that punishment.
Grammar and law both close a matter.
branches.cn: 语法与法律都在了结一件事。

branches.cn: 判决与宣判共用一个名称。

intro.cn: sentence 属于拉丁语 sentire（感觉、判断）词族。

definition_zh: 分开的；单独的；分开；分离
definition_en: not joined together, existing on its own, to divide things, or to move apart
core_image: 一条线把一张纸从中间裁开，两半各自落到桌上
scene: 老师把学生分成不同的小组。The teacher separated the students into different groups.
sceneCN: 这里 separated 是「分开」（第 3 个义项）；句意：老师把学生分成不同的小组。

senses.title: Not joined
senses.definition: not joined or connected to something else
senses.definitionCN: 没有与其他事物连在一起
senses.example: The twins sleep in separate beds.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎睡在不同的床上。
senses.why: This is the basic adjective sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的形容词义。

senses.title: On its own
senses.definition: existing or used on its own
senses.definitionCN: 独立存在或单独使用
senses.example: Each room has a separate entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 每个房间都有单独的入口。
senses.why: Being apart makes something distinct.
senses.whyCN: 彼此分开使事物各自独立。

senses.title: To divide
senses.definition: to divide people or things into groups
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物分成组
senses.example: The teacher separated the students into different groups.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把学生分成不同的小组。
senses.why: The adjective turns into the act of dividing.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为分开的动作。

senses.title: To move apart
senses.definition: to move apart or stop living together
senses.definitionCN: 彼此离开或不再共同生活
senses.example: The couple separated last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妻去年春天分居了。
senses.why: People and paths can separate too.
senses.whyCN: 人与道路也可以分离。

intro.en: Separate comes from Latin separare, from se-, apart, and parare, to prepare.
intro.cn: separate 出自拉丁语 separare，由 se-（分开）与 parare（准备）构成。

items.en: Se- meant apart.
items.cn: se- 意为分开。

items.en: Parare meant to prepare or arrange.
items.cn: parare 意为准备或安排。

items.en: Separare meant to set apart.
items.cn: separare 意为使分开。

items.en: English separate covered both the adjective and the verb.
items.cn: 英语 separate 兼作形容词与动词。

items.en: The spelling kept one form for both uses.
items.cn: 拼写保留了两种词性共用的一个形式。

note.en: Separate is compared with similar-looking words and with words for dividing.
note.cn: 把 separate 与形近词以及表示分开的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Separate means set apart, whether as an adjective or an action.
normalIntro.cn: separate 意为使分开，无论作形容词还是动词。

normal.en: The adjective ends with a soft sound.
normal.cn: 形容词形式的结尾发音较轻。

normal.en: The verb ends with the sound of ate.
normal.cn: 动词形式的结尾读作 ate 的音。

normal.en: Separate the white clothes from the dark.
normal.cn: 把浅色衣服与深色衣服分开。

normal.en: They keep separate accounts.
The couple separated after ten years.
normal.cn: 这对夫妻十年后分居了。

abstract.en: To name a thing is to set it apart.
abstract.cn: 给事物命名，就是把它区分出来。

abstract.en: Some things grow stronger when kept apart.
abstract.cn: 有些事物分开后反而更强。

abstract.en: A line divides the page but joins the story.
abstract.cn: 一条线分开纸页，却连起故事。

examples.en: The teacher separated the students into different groups.
examples.cn: 老师把学生分成不同的小组。

examples.en: Each room has a separate entrance.
examples.cn: 每个房间都有单独的入口。

examples.en: The couple separated last spring.
examples.cn: 这对夫妻去年春天分居了。

dict_mnemonic.text: separate 出自拉丁语 separare（使分开），由 se-（分开）与 parare（安排）构成，本义「分别安置」，兼作形容词与动词。

root: 源自拉丁语 separare，由 se-（分开）与 parare（安排）构成，核心义「分别安置」。

sensesIntro.en: Separate means not joined, existing alone, to divide, or to move apart.
sensesIntro.cn: separate 意为分开的、单独的、分开或分离。

core.en: Things set apart from one another.
core.cn: 彼此被分开的事物。

branches.en: Two things no longer joined.
One thing standing on its own.
The act of dividing a group.
branches.cn: 把一个群体分开的动作。

branches.en: Two people or paths moving apart.
branches.cn: 两个人或两条路彼此远离。

branches.en: Being apart and making apart share one word.
branches.cn: 分开的状态与动作共用一个词。

intro.en: Separate belongs to the Latin parare family of preparing and arranging.
intro.cn: separate 属于拉丁语 parare（准备、安排）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin separare and parare are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 separare 与 parare 是历史词根。

items.example: The filter is separating the oil.

definition_zh: 顺序；一系列；序列；按顺序排列
definition_en: the order in which things follow each other, a set of related events or items, or to arrange things in order
core_image: 一排骨牌依次倒下，前一块刚碰到后一块
scene: 数字按从小到大的顺序排列。The numbers are arranged in sequence from small to large.
sceneCN: 这里 sequence 是「顺序」（第 1 个义项）；句意：数字按从小到大的顺序排列。

senses.title: Order
senses.definition: the order in which things follow one another
senses.definitionCN: 事物一个接一个出现的次序
senses.example: The numbers are arranged in sequence from small to large.
senses.exampleCN: 数字按从小到大的顺序排列。
senses.why: This is the basic order sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的次序义。

senses.title: A series
senses.definition: a set of related events or things that follow each other
senses.definitionCN: 依次发生的一组相关事件或事物
senses.example: A sequence of storms hit the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 一连串风暴袭击了海岸。
senses.why: Order repeated becomes a series.
senses.whyCN: 次序反复出现就成为系列。

senses.title: Coded order
senses.definition: the ordered string of units in a code such as DNA
senses.definitionCN: 如 DNA 等编码中有序排列的单元串
senses.example: Scientists read the DNA sequence.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家读取了 DNA 序列。
senses.why: The order sense becomes technical.
senses.whyCN: 次序义在技术领域具体化。

senses.title: To put in order
senses.definition: to arrange items in a particular order
senses.definitionCN: 按特定次序安排项目
senses.example: They sequenced the files by date.
senses.exampleCN: 他们按日期给文件排序。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of ordering.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为排序的动作。

intro.en: Sequence comes from Latin sequentia, a following, from sequi, to follow.
intro.cn: sequence 出自拉丁语 sequentia（跟随），源于 sequi（跟随）。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随。

items.en: Sequentia named a following or succession.
items.cn: sequentia 指跟随或连续。

items.en: Old French sequence kept the order sense.
items.cn: 古法语 sequence 保留了次序义。

items.en: English sequence named a series of things.
items.cn: 英语 sequence 指一系列事物。

items.en: It extended to codes and computing.
items.cn: 它扩展到编码与计算领域。

note.en: Sequence is compared with similar-looking words and with words for order and series.
note.cn: 把 sequence 与形近词以及表示顺序、系列的词作比较。

entries.definition: a set of related things in order
a number of things following one another

normalIntro.en: Sequence is the order in which one thing follows another.
normalIntro.cn: sequence 是一个事物跟随另一个事物的次序。

normal.en: Sequence comes from the Latin word to follow.
normal.cn: sequence 出自拉丁语中表示跟随的词。

normal.en: Put the cards in the right sequence.
normal.cn: 把卡片按正确顺序摆好。

normal.en: A sequence of events explains a story.
normal.cn: 事件的先后顺序讲清一个故事。

normal.en: DNA sequence is a coded order.
normal.cn: DNA 序列是一种编码次序。

normal.en: The adjective is sequential.

abstract.en: Order is what turns separate moments into a story.
abstract.cn: 次序把分散的瞬间变成一个故事。

abstract.en: What follows depends on what came before.
abstract.cn: 后发生的事取决于先发生的事。

abstract.en: A long chain is held together by small links.
abstract.cn: 长链由小小的环节连成。

examples.en: The numbers are arranged in sequence from small to large.
examples.cn: 数字按从小到大的顺序排列。

examples.en: A sequence of storms hit the coast.
examples.cn: 一连串风暴袭击了海岸。

examples.en: Scientists read the DNA sequence.
examples.cn: 科学家读取了 DNA 序列。

dict_mnemonic.text: sequence 出自拉丁语 sequi（跟随），经 sequentia（连续），本义「一个接一个」，后指顺序、系列与序列。

intro.en: Sequence belongs to the Latin sequi family of following.

definition_zh: 系列；连续；丛书；电视系列片
definition_en: a number of similar things that come one after another, a set of books or programmes, or a group of sports games
core_image: 书架上同一套书按编号排成一列，书脊颜色一致
scene: 她看完了整部电视系列剧。She watched the whole television series.
sceneCN: 这里 series 是「电视系列片」（第 4 个义项）；句意：她看完了整部电视系列剧。

senses.title: Set of related things
senses.definition: a number of similar things that come one after another
senses.definitionCN: 一个接一个出现的一组相似事物
senses.example: The museum holds a series of paintings.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆藏有一系列画作。
senses.why: This is the basic set sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的一组事物义。

senses.title: Succession
senses.definition: a succession of events of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类事件接连发生
senses.example: A series of storms hit the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 一连串风暴袭击了海岸。
senses.why: The set is understood in time.
senses.whyCN: 这一组事物按时间理解。

senses.title: Set of books
senses.definition: a set of books published together
senses.definitionCN: 成套出版的书籍
senses.example: The library bought the whole series.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆买下了整套丛书。
senses.why: Published sets are called series.
senses.whyCN: 成套出版物称为 series。

senses.title: TV or sports series
senses.definition: a set of programmes or games that share a name
senses.definitionCN: 同名的一组节目或比赛
senses.example: She watched the whole television series.
senses.exampleCN: 她看完了整部电视系列剧。
senses.why: The set sense extends to broadcast and sport.
senses.whyCN: 组义扩展到广播与体育。

items.en: Series meant a row or chain.

items.en: It extended to books and broadcasts.

items.en: The plural form stayed series.

normal.en: One series, two series.

normal.en: A series of letters arrived.
The TV series has ten episodes.
normal.cn: 这部电视系列剧有十集。

normal.en: The library owns the whole series.
Serial means arranged in a series.
normal.cn: serial 意为按系列排列的。

abstract.en: One thing after another becomes a pattern.

abstract.en: A series lets a small story grow chapter by chapter.

abstract.en: Repetition with change holds attention.

examples.en: She watched the whole television series.

examples.en: The library bought the whole series.

core.en: Related things joined one after another.

branches.en: A set of similar items.

branches.en: Books published as a set.
Programmes or games under one name.

definition_zh: 服务；公共设施；服役；维修；发球
definition_en: work done for others, a public system such as transport, military duty, the act of maintaining a machine, or a tennis serve

scene: 顾客对这里的服务非常满意。The customers are very happy with the service.

senses.title: Work for others
senses.definition: work done to help customers or others
senses.definitionCN: 为顾客或他人提供的帮助性工作
senses.example: The customers are very happy with the service.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客对这里的服务非常满意。
senses.why: This is the core modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代核心义。

senses.title: Public system
senses.definition: a system that supplies a public need
senses.definitionCN: 满足公共需求的系统
senses.example: The bus service runs every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 公交服务每小时一班。

senses.title: Military duty
senses.definition: time spent in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 在军队中度过的时间
senses.example: He completed his military service.
senses.exampleCN: 他完成了兵役。

senses.title: Maintenance

senses.definitionCN: 检查与修理机器的行为

senses.why: Keeping a machine working is a service.
senses.whyCN: 保持机器运转是一种服务。

senses.title: Tennis serve
senses.definition: the act of starting play by hitting the ball
senses.definitionCN: 击球开始比赛的动作
senses.example: Her service won the game.
senses.exampleCN: 她的发球赢下了这一局。
senses.why: The opening stroke is also named service.
senses.whyCN: 开球动作也叫 service。

items.en: Servus meant slave or servant.
items.cn: servus 意为奴隶或仆人。

items.en: Servitium meant service or slavery.

items.en: Old French servise kept the service sense.

normal.cn: 良好的服务让顾客回头。

normal.en: A bus service is a public system.
normal.cn: 公交服务是一种公共系统。

normal.en: Military service is a duty to the state.
A service station repairs cars.
In tennis, service starts the point.

abstract.en: A society is held together by services people rarely see.
abstract.cn: 社会由人们很少看见的服务维系。

abstract.en: Maintenance is service to the future.
abstract.cn: 维护是对未来的服务。

abstract.en: To serve well is to make another's task lighter.
abstract.cn: 好好服务，就是让别人的事情变轻。

examples.en: The customers are very happy with the service.

examples.en: The bus service runs every hour.

sensesIntro.en: Service means work for others, a public system, military duty, maintenance, or a tennis serve.
sensesIntro.cn: service 意为服务、公共设施、服役、维修或发球。

core.en: Work and systems that serve a need.

branches.en: Help given to a customer.
A system that serves the public.
Time given to the armed forces.
Care that keeps a machine running.
Personal help and public systems share one word.
branches.cn: 个人帮助与公共系统共用一个词。

intro.en: Service belongs to the Latin servus family of service and duty.
intro.cn: service 属于拉丁语 servus（奴仆）词族，关联服务与职责。

latinIntro.en: Latin servitium and servus are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 servitium 与 servus 是历史词根。

items.exampleCN: 这家公司提供许多服务。

That advice did him a disservice.

definition_zh: 会议；一场；一节；会话
definition_en: a formal meeting, a period of an activity, a period of study, or a period of use of a computer system
core_image: 长桌旁，人们依次坐下，会议记录翻到新的一页
scene: 委员会在周一召开了一次会议。The committee held a session on Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 session 是「会议」（第 1 个义项）；句意：委员会在周一召开了一次会议。

senses.title: Formal meeting
senses.definition: a formal meeting of a group or official body
senses.definitionCN: 团体或官方机构的正式会议
senses.example: The committee held a session on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在周一召开了一次会议。
senses.why: This is the most common formal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常见的正式义项。

senses.title: Period of activity
senses.definition: a period of time used for one activity
senses.definitionCN: 用于某项活动的一段时间
senses.example: The band played a long session.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队演奏了很长时间。
senses.why: An activity can fill a sitting.
senses.whyCN: 一项活动可以占满一次「坐定」的时间。

senses.title: Period of study
senses.definition: a period of study at a school or university
senses.definitionCN: 学校或大学里的一节课、一个学期时段
senses.example: The summer session begins in June.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季学期在六月开始。
senses.why: Teaching is organized in sittings.
senses.whyCN: 教学按一个个时段来组织。

senses.title: Computer session
senses.definition: a period of use of a computer system
senses.definitionCN: 使用计算机系统的一段时间
senses.example: Save your work before ending the session.
senses.exampleCN: 结束会话前请保存工作。
senses.why: A login is a modern kind of sitting.
senses.whyCN: 登录是现代的「坐定」形式。

intro.en: Session comes from Latin sessio, a sitting, from sedere, to sit.
intro.cn: session 源自拉丁语 sessio（坐、会期），来自动词 sedere（坐）。

items.en: Sedere meant to sit.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐。

items.en: Sessio meant a sitting or a meeting.
items.cn: sessio 意为坐、会期。

items.en: Session kept the sense of a sitting.
items.cn: session 保留了「坐定开会」的含义。

items.en: Session named a formal meeting.
items.cn: session 指正式会议。

items.en: Session extended to study and computers.
items.cn: session 扩展到学期时段与计算机会话。

note.en: Session is compared with similar-looking words and with words for meetings.
note.cn: 把 session 与形近词以及表示会议的字词作比较。

the giving up of land or rights

normalIntro.en: Session is a period defined by people sitting down together to do something.
normalIntro.cn: session 是一段由人们坐下来共同做事所定义的时间。

normal.en: The court is now in session.
Each training session lasts an hour.
normal.cn: 每节培训课持续一小时。

normal.en: The band had a late-night session.
normal.cn: 乐队进行了一场深夜演奏。

normal.en: The summer session has three courses.
Log out to close your session.

abstract.en: To sit together is to give a moment a shared shape.
abstract.cn: 坐在一起，就是给一段时间一个共同的形状。

abstract.en: Every meeting is a small stage with a beginning and an end.
abstract.cn: 每一场会议都是有小幕起落的小舞台。

abstract.en: A session ends, but what was decided may keep standing.
abstract.cn: 会期会结束，但作出的决定可能一直立着。

examples.en: The committee held a session on Monday.
examples.cn: 委员会在周一召开了一次会议。

examples.en: The band played a long session.
examples.cn: 乐队演奏了很长时间。

examples.en: Save your work before ending the session.
examples.cn: 结束会话前请保存工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: session 源自拉丁语 sedere（坐），核心义「坐下来的一段时间」，引申为会议、会期与会话。

root: 源自拉丁语 sedere（坐）的名词 sessio（坐、会期）。

sensesIntro.en: Session means a formal meeting, a period of activity, a term of study, or a computer login period.
sensesIntro.cn: session 意为正式会议、一场活动、学期时段或计算机会话。

core.en: A period shaped by people sitting together.
core.cn: 由人们坐在一起所形成的一段时间。

branches.en: An official gathering.
A stretch of one activity.
A school or university term.
branches.cn: 学校或大学的一个学期时段。

branches.en: A period inside a computer system.
branches.cn: 在计算机系统里的一段使用时间。

branches.en: Meeting and activity share a sitting.
branches.cn: 会议与活动都落在一次「坐定」里。

intro.en: Session is built on the Latin root sed-, sit, with the noun suffix -ion.
intro.cn: session 建立在拉丁词根 sed-（坐）之上，加名词后缀 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin sedere, to sit, also gave sedentary and sediment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere（坐）也孕育了 sedentary 与 sediment。

items.example: Sessional work is paid by the hour.

definition_zh: 放置；设置；树立；凝固；一套
definition_en: to put something in place, to adjust equipment, to establish something, to become solid, or a group of things used together
core_image: 闹钟被放到床头，指针停在六点
scene: 她把花瓶放在桌上。She set the vase on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 set 是「放置」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她把花瓶放在桌上。

senses.title: To place
senses.definition: to put something in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到特定位置
senses.example: She set the vase on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 她把花瓶放在桌上。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: To adjust
senses.definition: to adjust a device or arrange something in advance
senses.definitionCN: 调整装置或预先安排好
senses.example: He set the alarm for six.
senses.exampleCN: 他把闹钟设在六点。
senses.why: Setting a device is placing its state.
senses.whyCN: 设置装置就是安放它的状态。

senses.title: To establish
senses.definition: to establish a record, rule, or example
senses.definitionCN: 创下纪录、定下规则或树立榜样
senses.example: The team set a new record.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍创下了新纪录。
senses.why: An idea can be placed firmly too.
senses.whyCN: 观念也能被牢牢安放。

senses.title: To become solid
senses.definition: to become solid or fixed
senses.definitionCN: 变成固体或固定下来
senses.example: The jelly will set in the fridge.
senses.exampleCN: 果冻会在冰箱里凝固。
senses.why: A liquid takes a fixed shape.
senses.whyCN: 液体固定成一种形状。

senses.title: A group of things
senses.definition: a group of things that belong together
senses.definitionCN: 配套的一组东西
senses.example: She bought a set of tools.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一套工具。
senses.why: The noun names things placed together.
senses.whyCN: 名词指被放在一起的一组东西。

intro.en: Set comes from Old English settan, to cause to sit, from the same root as sit.
intro.cn: set 源自古英语 settan（使坐下），与 sit 同根。

items.en: Satjan meant to cause to sit.
items.cn: satjan 意为使坐下。

items.en: Settan meant to place or set.
items.cn: settan 意为放置、安放。

items.en: Set kept its placing sense.
items.cn: set 保留了放置的含义。

items.en: Set extended to devices and records.
items.cn: set 扩展到装置设置与纪录。

items.en: The noun named a matched group.
items.cn: 名词形式指配套的一组。

note.en: Set is compared with similar-looking words and with words for placing.
note.cn: 把 set 与形近词以及表示放置的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Set is the act of causing something to sit: an object, a clock, a record, or a liquid.
normalIntro.cn: set 就是让某物「坐下」：一个物件、一只钟、一项纪录或一种液体。

normal.en: Set the cup on the shelf.
Set the alarm before bed.
They set a record in the relay.
normal.cn: 他们在接力赛中创下纪录。

normal.en: Leave the cement to set.
This set of dishes has six plates.
normal.cn: 这套餐具共有六个盘子。

abstract.en: To set something is to decide where it belongs.
abstract.cn: 安放某物，就是决定它该在哪里。

abstract.en: A record is a moment set into history.
abstract.cn: 纪录，是被安放进历史的一刻。

abstract.en: Some things set only when we stop holding them.
abstract.cn: 有些东西，只有我们松手后才会定型。

examples.en: She set the vase on the table.
examples.cn: 她把花瓶放在桌上。

examples.en: He set the alarm for six.
examples.cn: 他把闹钟设在六点。

examples.en: The jelly will set in the fridge.
examples.cn: 果冻会在冰箱里凝固。

dict_mnemonic.text: set 源自古英语 settan（使坐下），核心义「把东西安放到某个位置」，引申出设置、树立、凝固与一套。

root: 源自古英语 settan（使坐下、安放），与 sit 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Set means to place, adjust, establish, become solid, or a matched group.
sensesIntro.cn: set 意为放置、设置、树立、凝固或一套。

core.en: Causing something to take a fixed place.
core.cn: 使某物占据一个固定的位置。

branches.en: Putting an object down.
Arranging a device.
Fixing a record or rule.
A liquid taking shape.
Things placed together.
branches.cn: 被放在一起的一组东西。

intro.en: Set is a short native verb that joins with prefixes to make many new words.
intro.cn: set 是简短的日耳曼语本族动词，能与前缀组合出许多新词。

latinIntro.en: Set has no Latin ancestor; Latin ponere, to place, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: set 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 ponere（放置）只是语义对应词。

items.example: She sets the table every night.
The story has a rural setting.
The oven is preset to 180 degrees.
items.exampleCN: 烤箱预设为一百八十度。

items.example: Reset the clock after the power cut.

items.meaning: to balance one effect with another
items.exampleCN: 节省抵消了更高的成本。

items.example: The setter placed the ball well.

definition_zh: 定居；解决；安顿；沉降
definition_en: to live permanently somewhere, to end an argument or problem, to make oneself comfortable, or to sink slowly
core_image: 行李放在新家的地板上，窗外的路终于不再延伸
scene: 他们在一个小镇定居下来。They settled in a small town.
sceneCN: 这里 settle 是「定居」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们在一个小镇定居下来。

senses.title: To live permanently
senses.definition: to go and live permanently in a place
senses.definitionCN: 到某地永久居住下来
senses.example: They settled in a small town.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一个小镇定居下来。
senses.why: This is the main modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代主要义项。

senses.title: To resolve
senses.definition: to end an argument or solve a problem
senses.definitionCN: 结束争论或解决问题
senses.example: The two sides settled the dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 双方解决了争端。
senses.why: A matter comes to rest.
senses.whyCN: 事情落定下来。

senses.title: To get comfortable
senses.definition: to make oneself comfortable in a place
senses.definitionCN: 在某处安顿舒服
senses.example: She settled into the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 她在椅子上安顿下来。
senses.why: The body finds its place.
senses.whyCN: 身体找到自己的位置。

senses.title: To sink down
senses.definition: to sink slowly to the bottom or onto a surface
senses.definitionCN: 慢慢沉到底部或落在表面
senses.example: The dust settled on the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘落在架子上。
senses.why: Even particles come to rest.
senses.whyCN: 连微粒也会落定。

intro.en: Settle comes from Old English setlan, to seat, from setl, a seat.
intro.cn: settle 源自古英语 setlan（使就座），来自 setl（座位）。

items.en: Setl meant a seat.
items.cn: setl 意为座位。

items.en: Setlan meant to seat or place.
items.cn: setlan 意为使就座、安放。

items.en: Settle meant to come to rest.
items.cn: settle 意为落定、安定。

items.en: Settle named permanent residence.
items.cn: settle 指定居。

items.en: Settle extended to disputes and debts.
items.cn: settle 扩展到解决争端与清偿债务。

note.en: Settle is compared with similar-looking words and with words for resolving and residing.
note.cn: 把 settle 与形近词以及表示解决和居住的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Settle is the body, the argument, and the dust all finding a place to rest.
normalIntro.cn: settle 是身体、争论与灰尘都找到地方安歇。

normal.en: They settled near the river.
The quarrel was settled quickly.
She settled into a warm chair.
normal.cn: 她在温暖的椅子上安顿下来。

normal.en: Snow settled on the roof.
The bill was settled by card.

abstract.en: To settle is to stop moving long enough to belong.
abstract.cn: 安顿下来，就是停得够久，从而有所归属。

abstract.en: Some arguments end not by winning but by resting.
abstract.cn: 有些争论不是赢出来的，而是停下来才结束的。

abstract.en: Everything heavy eventually finds the ground.
abstract.cn: 沉重之物终会找到地面。

examples.en: They settled in a small town.
examples.cn: 他们在一个小镇定居下来。

examples.en: The two sides settled the dispute.
examples.cn: 双方解决了争端。

examples.en: The dust settled on the shelf.
examples.cn: 灰尘落在架子上。

dict_mnemonic.text: settle 源自古英语 setlan（使就座），核心义「坐下来、安定」，引申出定居、解决与沉降。

root: 源自古英语 setl（座位）与 setlan（使就座），核心义「安放到座位上」。

sensesIntro.en: Settle means to live somewhere, resolve a problem, get comfortable, or sink down.
sensesIntro.cn: settle 意为定居、解决、安顿或沉降。

core.en: Coming to rest in a place or a condition.
core.cn: 在某个位置或状态中安定下来。

branches.en: Staying in one place.
Bringing a dispute to rest.
The body finding comfort.
Particles coming to the bottom.
Home and comfort share one verb.
branches.cn: 安家与安适共用一个动词。

intro.en: Settle grows from the old seat word setl and its suffix -le.
intro.cn: settle 从古老的「座位」词 setl 加后缀 -le 生长而来。

latinIntro.en: Settle has no Latin ancestor; Latin sedere, to sit, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: settle 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 sedere（坐）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The bird settled on the branch.

items.meaning: the act of coming to rest

items.exampleCN: 土壤的沉降花了几个月。

items.example: The first settlers built a bridge.
items.exampleCN: 最早的定居者建了一座桥。

items.example: The family resettled in the north.
items.exampleCN: 这家人重新在北方定居。

definition_zh: 严厉的；严峻的；朴素的
definition_en: very strict or harsh, very serious or dangerous, or plain and without decoration
core_image: 暴雨砸在窗上，树枝被风压得几乎折断
scene: 暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。The storm caused severe damage.
sceneCN: 这里 severe 是「严峻的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。

senses.title: Strict and harsh
senses.definition: very strict or harsh in treatment or judgment
senses.definitionCN: 在对待或评判上非常严格、苛刻的
senses.example: The judge gave a severe warning.
senses.exampleCN: 法官给出了严厉的警告。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义。

senses.title: Very serious
senses.definition: very serious or dangerous
senses.definitionCN: 非常严重或危险的
senses.example: The storm caused severe damage.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。
senses.why: Danger is strict in its own way.
senses.whyCN: 危险也有它自己的严厉。

senses.title: Plain and simple
senses.definition: plain and without decoration
senses.definitionCN: 朴素、不加装饰的
senses.example: The room was clean and severe.
senses.exampleCN: 房间干净而朴素。
senses.why: A severe style allows nothing extra.
senses.whyCN: 朴素的风格不允许任何多余。

intro.en: Severe comes from Latin severus, serious and strict, through Old French.
intro.cn: severe 源自拉丁语 severus（严肃、严格），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Severus meant serious and strict.
items.cn: severus 意为严肃而严格。

items.en: Severitas named strictness.
items.cn: severitas 指严格。

items.en: Severe meant harsh or strict.
items.cn: severe 意为严厉或严格。

items.en: Severe described strict judgment.
items.cn: severe 描述严格的评判。

items.en: Severe extended to serious conditions and plain style.
items.cn: severe 扩展到严峻的状况与朴素的风格。

note.en: Severe is compared with similar-looking words and with words for harshness.
note.cn: 把 severe 与形近词以及表示严厉的词作比较。

entries.definition: more than two but not many

normalIntro.en: Severe is a line drawn hard: strict rules, serious harm, plain style.
normalIntro.cn: severe 是一条画得很硬的线：严格的规则、严重的伤害、朴素的风格。

normal.en: The drought was severe.
He felt severe pain in his back.
The school has severe rules.
The building has a severe design.
The severest winter in years came.
normal.cn: 多年来最严酷的冬天来了。

abstract.en: A severe line cuts away everything unnecessary.
abstract.cn: 严厉的线条，会削去一切多余。

abstract.en: What is serious cannot be softened by ignoring it.
abstract.cn: 严重的事，不能靠忽视来减轻。

abstract.en: Plainness can be a kind of strength.
abstract.cn: 朴素，也可以是一种力量。

examples.en: The storm caused severe damage.
examples.cn: 暴风雨造成了严重的破坏。

examples.en: The judge gave a severe warning.
examples.cn: 法官给出了严厉的警告。

examples.en: The room was clean and severe.
examples.cn: 房间干净而朴素。

dict_mnemonic.text: severe 源自拉丁语 severus（严肃、严格），核心义「不留余地的严」，引申为严重与朴素。

root: 源自拉丁语 severus（严肃、严格），核心义「毫不宽松」。

sensesIntro.en: Severe means strict, very serious, or plain and undecorated.
sensesIntro.cn: severe 意为严厉的、严峻的或朴素的。

core.en: A quality that allows no softness or excess.
core.cn: 不容松懈、不容多余的特质。

branches.en: Strict treatment or judgment.
A situation that is very bad.
A style without decoration.
Harshness in people and in events.
Serious conditions and plain forms both cut away ease.
branches.cn: 严峻的处境与朴素的形式，都削去了安逸。

intro.en: Severe is a Latin adjective whose family includes severity and persevere.
intro.cn: severe 是拉丁语形容词，其词族包括 severity 与 persevere。

latinIntro.en: The Latin severus, serious, also lies behind persevere, to persist strictly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 severus（严肃）也是 persevere（严格坚持）的词源基础。

items.example: This winter is severer than last.
items.exampleCN: 这个冬天比去年更严酷。

items.example: It was the severest test of the year.
items.exampleCN: 这是全年最严峻的考验。

items.example: The severity of the storm surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 暴风雨的猛烈让我们吃惊。

items.example: The severeness of his tone was clear.

items.exampleCN: 尽管遭遇挫折，她仍坚持不懈。

definition_zh: 阴凉处；色调；灯罩；遮挡光线
definition_en: an area away from direct sunlight, a particular degree of colour, a cover that softens a light, or to shelter something from light
core_image: 树冠下的一块暗地，光斑在草叶上晃动
scene: 我们坐在树荫下。We sat in the shade of a tree.
sceneCN: 这里 shade 是「阴凉处」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我们坐在树荫下。

senses.title: Area out of sunlight
senses.definition: a place where direct sunlight is blocked
senses.definitionCN: 直射阳光被挡住的地方
senses.example: We sat in the shade of a tree.
senses.exampleCN: 我们坐在树荫下。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most common sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老、最常见的义项。

senses.title: Degree of colour
senses.definition: a particular degree or variety of a colour
senses.definitionCN: 颜色的某种深浅或变化
senses.example: The walls are a pale shade of blue.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁是淡蓝色调。
senses.why: Darkness and colour are both degrees of light.
senses.whyCN: 暗度与颜色都是光的程度。

senses.title: Lamp cover
senses.definition: a cover that softens or directs a light
senses.definitionCN: 使光线变柔或改变方向的罩子
senses.example: She bought a new lamp shade.
senses.exampleCN: 她买了一个新灯罩。
senses.why: A shade controls light indoors.
senses.whyCN: 灯罩在室内控制光线。

senses.title: To block light
senses.definition: to shelter something from direct light
senses.definitionCN: 使某物免受直射光
senses.example: The trees shade the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 树木为花园遮阴。
senses.why: The noun becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为动作。

intro.en: Shade comes from Old English sceadu, shadow, and is closely related to shadow.
intro.cn: shade 源自古英语 sceadu（影子），与 shadow 关系密切。

items.en: Skadwo meant shadow.
items.cn: skadwo 意为影子。

items.en: Sceadu meant shade or shadow.
items.cn: sceadu 意为阴凉或影子。

items.en: Shade named shelter from the sun.
items.cn: shade 指遮阳的阴凉处。

items.en: Shade named degrees of colour.
items.cn: shade 指颜色的深浅。

items.en: Shade named a lamp cover.
items.cn: shade 指灯罩。

note.en: Shade is compared with similar-looking words and with words for shadow and colour.
note.cn: 把 shade 与形近词以及表示影子和颜色的词作比较。

entries.definition: a dark shape cast by an object

normalIntro.en: Shade is light held back: under a tree, inside a colour, over a lamp.
normalIntro.cn: shade 是被挡住的光：在树下、在颜色里、在灯上。

normal.en: The dog slept in the shade.
The sofa is a darker shade of grey.
normal.cn: 沙发是更深一层的灰色。

normal.en: The lamp shade is made of paper.
A large tree shades the road.
There are many shades of meaning here.
normal.cn: 这里有意义上的许多细微差别。

abstract.en: Shade is the shape light leaves when it is interrupted.
abstract.cn: 阴凉，是光被打断后留下的形状。

abstract.en: Every colour is a small decision about how much light to keep.
abstract.cn: 每一种颜色，都是关于保留多少光的小决定。

abstract.en: Rest often happens just outside the brightest place.
abstract.cn: 休息，常常发生在最亮处之外。

examples.en: We sat in the shade of a tree.
examples.cn: 我们坐在树荫下。

examples.en: The walls are a pale shade of blue.
examples.cn: 墙壁是淡蓝色调。

examples.en: She bought a new lamp shade.
examples.cn: 她买了一个新灯罩。

sensesIntro.cn: shade 意为阴凉处、色调、灯罩或遮挡光线。

core.en: Light partly blocked, creating rest or tone.
core.cn: 光被部分挡住，产生阴凉或色调。

The act of blocking light.

intro.en: Shade is a native Germanic word that builds shadow and shady.
intro.cn: shade 是日耳曼语本族词，衍生出 shadow 与 shady。

items.example: We rested on a shady bench.
items.exampleCN: 我们在阴凉的长椅上休息。

items.meaning: a dark shape cast by light
items.example: The shadow moved with the sun.
A shadowy figure stood at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 一个朦胧的身影站在门口。
这个消息让聚会黯然失色。

definition_zh: 浅的；浅薄的；浅呼吸的
definition_en: not deep, not showing serious thought, or breathing with little air
core_image: 目光穿过清澈的浅水，直接看到河底的卵石
scene: 孩子们在浅水里玩耍。The children played in the shallow water.
sceneCN: 这里 shallow 是「浅的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子们在浅水里玩耍。

senses.title: Not deep
senses.definition: having only a short distance from top to bottom
senses.definitionCN: 从上到下的距离很短的
senses.example: The children played in the shallow water.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在浅水里玩耍。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Not serious
senses.definition: lacking deep thought or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏深刻思想或感情的
senses.example: The book offers only a shallow view.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书只给出浅薄的看法。
senses.why: Depth of water became a metaphor for depth of mind.
senses.whyCN: 水的深度被隐喻为思想的深度。

senses.title: Light breathing
senses.definition: taking in only a little air
senses.definitionCN: 只吸入少量空气的
senses.example: He was breathing in shallow breaths.
senses.exampleCN: 他在浅呼吸。
senses.why: Each breath goes only a little way down.
senses.whyCN: 每次呼吸只进入很浅的位置。

senses.title: Shallows
senses.definition: an area of shallow water
senses.definitionCN: 水浅的区域
senses.example: The boat stuck in the shallows.
senses.exampleCN: 船搁浅在浅滩上。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for such a place.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为指这种地点的名词。

intro.cn: shallow 出现于中古英语晚期，可能与古英语中表示浅滩的词有关。

items.en: Sceald named a shoal or shallow place.
items.cn: sceald 指浅滩或水浅处。

items.en: Schalowe meant not deep.
items.cn: schalowe 意为不深的。

items.en: Shallow described water and containers.
items.cn: shallow 描述水和容器。

items.en: The word described shallow breathing.
items.cn: 这个词描述浅呼吸。

items.en: Shallow became a metaphor for a light mind.
items.cn: shallow 成为思想浅薄的隐喻。

note.en: Shallow is compared with similar-looking words and with words for depth.
note.cn: 把 shallow 与形近词以及表示深度的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Shallow means close to the surface, in water, in breath, or in thought.
normalIntro.cn: shallow 意为靠近表面，无论是水、呼吸还是思想。

normal.en: The river is shallow here.
We waded through shallow water.
A shallow mind avoids hard questions.
His breathing was shallow.
The boat grounded in the shallows.

abstract.en: Shallow water is easy to cross and easy to see through.
abstract.cn: 浅水容易穿过，也容易看透。

abstract.en: Depth cannot be judged from the surface.
abstract.cn: 深度无法从表面判断。

abstract.en: A shallow answer often ends the question too early.
abstract.cn: 浅薄的回答常让问题过早结束。

examples.en: The children played in the shallow water.

examples.en: The book offers only a shallow view.

sensesIntro.en: Shallow means not deep in water, breath, or thought, or a shallow place.
sensesIntro.cn: shallow 意为水浅、呼吸浅、思想浅，或浅滩。

core.cn: 从表面到底部的距离很短。

branches.en: Water close to its bed.

Water and thought share the idea of depth.
